li.label: attended a feast
li.description: A real banquet, like in the tales. The hall, the meat, the mead, the company.

li.label: a thin colony feast
li.description: We sat down together, at least. The table could have been better.

li.label: a modest colony feast
li.description: Good food, good company and a night off.

li.label: a fine colony feast
li.description: A proper feast in our own hall. We needed that.

li.label: a colony feast to remember
li.description: The hall, the meat, the drink, the music. Nobody will forget that night.

li.label: a bare wake
li.description: We raised what little we had to their memory.

li.label: a decent wake
li.description: We sat together and spoke of the dead. It helped.

li.label: a fine wake
li.description: A full table and full cups for one of ours. They would have liked it.

li.label: a wake they deserved
li.description: The whole hall drank to their name. Nobody leaves this colony unsung.

li.label: a thin victory feast
li.description: We won, and there was not much to celebrate it with.

li.label: a modest victory feast
li.description: We held the walls, and we drank to it.

li.label: a fine victory feast
li.description: They came for us, and we are the ones feasting tonight.

li.label: a victory feast to remember
li.description: The hall roared. Let them come again.

li.label: a thin harvest feast
li.description: The stores are full, even if the table was not.

li.label: a modest harvest feast
li.description: A year of work, and a night to enjoy it.

li.label: a fine harvest feast
li.description: The granary is full and so are we.

li.label: a harvest feast to remember
li.description: Whatever winter brings, we ate like lords tonight.

li.label: won a drinking contest
li.description: I drank them under the table, and the whole hall saw it.

li.label: a night with a noble
li.description: Silks, a proper bed, and someone with clean hands and good manners for once. Say what you like about the nobility.

li.label: we broke the guest right
li.description: They ate at our table. They drank our mead. And we put them in the ground. Whatever we are now, we are no hosts.
